question: From the PostgreSQL manual (current release, plus the release that introduced each setting when the manual says so) and the source code: how a snapshot decides visibility; why the comparison horizon is about 2 billion XIDs; every setting that drives freezing (vacuum_freeze_min_age, vacuum_freeze_table_age, autovacuum_freeze_max_age, the MultiXact twins, the failsafe ages) with defaults, ranges and limits; the warnings and the hard stop the server applies as the limit nears, with their thresholds; the recovery procedure the manual prescribes once the stop is reached. Must find: exact values, modal verbs and version numbers.

facts.summary: The PostgreSQL 19 manual says MVCC depends on comparing XIDs: a row version whose inserting XID is greater than the current transaction's XID is in the future and should not be visible to it.
facts.quote: PostgreSQL's MVCC transaction semantics depend on being able to compare transaction ID (XID) numbers: a row version with an insertion XID greater than the current transaction's XID is “in the future” and should not be visible to the current transaction.

facts.summary: XIDs are 32 bits, so after more than 4 billion transactions the counter wraps to zero; to avoid this every table in every database must be vacuumed at least once every two billion transactions.
facts.quote: since transaction IDs have limited size (32 bits) a cluster that runs for a long time (more than 4 billion transactions) would suffer transaction ID wraparound: the XID counter wraps around to zero, and all of a sudden transactions that were in the past appear to be in the future … it is necessary to vacuum every table in every database at least once every two billion transactions.

facts.summary: Normal XIDs are compared with modulo-2^32 arithmetic (the saved text shows it as 'modulo-232', the superscript lost), so each normal XID has two billion older and two billion newer XIDs: the space is circular.
facts.quote: Normal XIDs are compared using modulo-232 arithmetic. This means that for every normal XID, there are two billion XIDs that are “older” and two billion that are “newer”; another way to say it is that the normal XID space is circular with no endpoint.

facts.summary: A row version created with a normal XID appears in the past for the next two billion transactions; if it still exists after more than two billion, it suddenly appears to be in the future.
facts.quote: once a row version has been created with a particular normal XID, the row version will appear to be “in the past” for the next two billion transactions, no matter which normal XID we are talking about. If the row version still exists after more than two billion transactions, it will suddenly appear to be in the future.

facts.summary: FrozenTransactionId is a reserved XID outside the normal comparison rules, always older than every normal XID; frozen row versions are treated as if inserted by it.
facts.quote: PostgreSQL reserves a special XID, FrozenTransactionId, which does not follow the normal XID comparison rules and is always considered older than every normal XID. Frozen row versions are treated as if the inserting XID were FrozenTransactionId

facts.summary: Before PostgreSQL 9.4 freezing replaced xmin with FrozenTransactionId; newer versions set a flag bit and keep xmin. FrozenTransactionId is the value 2, still seen in clusters pg_upgrade'd from pre-9.4.
facts.quote: In PostgreSQL versions before 9.4, freezing was implemented by actually replacing a row's insertion XID with FrozenTransactionId, which was visible in the row's xmin system column. Newer versions just set a flag bit, preserving the row's original xmin for possible forensic use. However, rows with xmin equal to FrozenTransactionId (2) may still be found in databases pg_upgrade'd from pre-9.4 versions.

facts.summary: BootstrapTransactionId is the value 1, found in catalog rows inserted during the first phase of initdb, and is also treated as older than every normal XID.
facts.quote: system catalogs may contain rows with xmin equal to BootstrapTransactionId (1), indicating that they were inserted during the first phase of initdb. Like FrozenTransactionId, this special XID is treated as older than every normal XID.

facts.summary: vacuum_freeze_min_age sets how old an XID must be before rows bearing it are frozen.
facts.quote: vacuum_freeze_min_age controls how old an XID value has to be before rows bearing that XID will be frozen.

facts.summary: Because VACUUM skips pages via the visibility map, normal vacuums may leave old rows unfrozen; an aggressive vacuum then freezes all eligible XIDs and MXIDs, including all-visible but not all-frozen pages.
facts.quote: normal VACUUMs won't always freeze every old row version in the table. When that happens, VACUUM will eventually need to perform an aggressive vacuum, which will freeze all eligible unfrozen XID and MXID values, including those from all-visible but not all-frozen pages.

facts.summary: vacuum_freeze_table_age decides when a table is vacuumed aggressively (age since the last such scan above vacuum_freeze_table_age minus vacuum_freeze_min_age); setting it to 0 makes every VACUUM aggressive.
facts.quote: vacuum_freeze_table_age controls when a table is aggressively vacuumed. All all-visible but not all-frozen pages are scanned if the number of transactions that have passed since the last such scan is greater than vacuum_freeze_table_age minus vacuum_freeze_min_age. Setting vacuum_freeze_table_age to 0 forces VACUUM to always use its aggressive strategy.

facts.summary: A table can go unvacuumed for at most two billion transactions minus vacuum_freeze_min_age; autovacuum is invoked on tables with unfrozen XIDs older than autovacuum_freeze_max_age, even when autovacuum is disabled.
facts.quote: The maximum time that a table can go unvacuumed is two billion transactions minus the vacuum_freeze_min_age value at the time of the last aggressive vacuum. … autovacuum is invoked on any table that might contain unfrozen rows with XIDs older than the age specified by the configuration parameter autovacuum_freeze_max_age. (This will happen even if autovacuum is disabled.)

facts.summary: The effective maximum of vacuum_freeze_table_age is 0.95 times autovacuum_freeze_max_age; higher settings are capped.
facts.quote: The effective maximum for vacuum_freeze_table_age is 0.95 * autovacuum_freeze_max_age; a setting higher than that will be capped to the maximum.

facts.summary: autovacuum_freeze_max_age has a maximum allowed value of two billion (pg_xact about half a gigabyte, pg_commit_ts about 20GB) and a default of 200 million (about 50MB of pg_xact, 2GB of pg_commit_ts).
facts.quote: if autovacuum_freeze_max_age is set to its maximum allowed value of two billion, pg_xact can be expected to grow to about half a gigabyte and pg_commit_ts to about 20GB. … (The default, 200 million transactions, translates to about 50MB of pg_xact storage and about 2GB of pg_commit_ts storage.)

facts.summary: relfrozenxid in pg_class holds the oldest unfrozen XID left after the last VACUUM that advanced it; datfrozenxid in pg_database is the minimum of the per-table relfrozenxid values.
facts.quote: the relfrozenxid column of a table's pg_class row contains the oldest remaining unfrozen XID at the end of the most recent VACUUM that successfully advanced relfrozenxid (typically the most recent aggressive VACUUM). Similarly, the datfrozenxid column of a database's pg_database row is a lower bound on the unfrozen XIDs appearing in that database — it is just the minimum of the per-table relfrozenxid values within the database.

facts.summary: Warnings start when the database's oldest XIDs are one hundred million transactions from the wraparound point; the manual shows the WARNING, DETAIL (percentage of XID space left) and HINT lines.
facts.quote: the system will begin to emit warning messages like this when the database's oldest XIDs reach one hundred million transactions from the wraparound point: … WARNING: database "mydb" must be vacuumed within 99985967 transactions DETAIL: Approximately 4.66% of transaction ID space remains before wraparound. HINT: To avoid transaction ID assignment failures, execute a database-wide VACUUM in that database.

facts.summary: The fixing VACUUM should be run by a superuser, else it cannot process system catalogs and advance datfrozenxid; if warnings are ignored the server refuses new XIDs once fewer than three million remain before wraparound.
facts.quote: note that the VACUUM should be performed by a superuser, else it will fail to process system catalogs, which prevent it from being able to advance the database's datfrozenxid.) If these warnings are ignored, the system will refuse to assign new XIDs once there are fewer than three million transactions left until wraparound:

facts.summary: The manual's example of the hard-stop error and its hint.
facts.quote: ERROR: database is not accepting commands that assign new transaction IDs to avoid wraparound data loss in database "mydb" HINT: Execute a database-wide VACUUM in that database.

facts.summary: In the stopped state, running transactions continue, only read-only transactions can start, writes and truncation fail, VACUUM still runs; stopping the postmaster or single-user mode is not necessary or desirable.
facts.quote: In this condition any transactions already in progress can continue, but only read-only transactions can be started. Operations that modify database records or truncate relations will fail. The VACUUM command can still be run normally. Note that, contrary to what was sometimes recommended in earlier releases, it is not necessary or desirable to stop the postmaster or enter single user-mode in order to restore normal operation.

facts.summary: Recovery steps 1 to 3: resolve old prepared transactions (pg_prepared_xacts), end long-running transactions (pg_stat_activity), drop old replication slots (pg_replication_slots), each found by a large age().
facts.quote: Resolve old prepared transactions. You can find these by checking pg_prepared_xacts for rows where age(transactionid) is large. Such transactions should be committed or rolled back. … End long-running open transactions. You can find these by checking pg_stat_activity for rows where age(backend_xid) or age(backend_xmin) is large. … Drop any old replication slots. Use pg_replication_slots to find slots where age(xmin) or age(catalog_xmin) is large.

facts.summary: Recovery step 4: run VACUUM in the target database (database-wide, or on the oldest tables; the page writes 'relminxid'); not VACUUM FULL, which needs an XID, and not VACUUM FREEZE; then check autovacuum's configuration.
facts.quote: Execute VACUUM in the target database. A database-wide VACUUM is simplest; to reduce the time required, it is also possible to issue manual VACUUM commands on the tables where relminxid is oldest. Do not use VACUUM FULL in this scenario, because it requires an XID and will therefore fail, except in super-user mode, where it will instead consume an XID and thus increase the risk of transaction ID wraparound. Do not use VACUUM FREEZE either … Once normal operation is restored, ensure that autovacuum is properly configured in the target database in order to avoid future problems.

facts.summary: Single-user mode, once sometimes needed, should be avoided: it takes the system down and disables the wraparound safeguards; its only use here is to TRUNCATE or DROP tables, which the three-million-transaction margin exists for.
facts.quote: In earlier versions, it was sometimes necessary to stop the postmaster and VACUUM the database in a single-user mode. In typical scenarios, this is no longer necessary, and should be avoided whenever possible, since it involves taking the system down. It is also riskier, since it disables transaction ID wraparound safeguards that are designed to prevent data loss. The only reason to use single-user mode in this scenario is if you wish to TRUNCATE or DROP unneeded tables to avoid needing to VACUUM them. The three-million-transaction safety margin exists to let the administrator do this.

facts.summary: VACUUM replaces multixact IDs older than vacuum_multixact_freeze_min_age; relminmxid holds the oldest multixact ID in a table, and when it is older than vacuum_multixact_freeze_table_age an aggressive vacuum is forced.
facts.quote: Whenever VACUUM scans any part of a table, it will replace any multixact ID it encounters which is older than vacuum_multixact_freeze_min_age by a different value, which can be the zero value, a single transaction ID, or a newer multixact ID. For each table, pg_class.relminmxid stores the oldest possible multixact ID still appearing in any tuple of that table. If this value is older than vacuum_multixact_freeze_table_age, an aggressive vacuum is forced.

facts.summary: An aggressive scan runs for any table whose multixact age exceeds autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age, even with autovacuum disabled; past about 2 billion member entries (about 10GB) aggressive scans run more often.
facts.quote: As a safety device, an aggressive vacuum scan will occur for any table whose multixact-age is greater than autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age. The aggressive scans will occur even if autovacuum is nominally disabled. Also, if the number of multixact member entries created exceeds approximately 2 billion entries (occupying roughly 10GB in the pg_multixact/members directory), aggressive vacuum scans will occur more often for all tables

facts.summary: MXIDs have the same thresholds: warnings at one hundred million from the wraparound point, refusal to generate new MXIDs below three million left.
facts.quote: if autovacuum fails to clear old MXIDs from a table, the system will begin to emit warning messages when the database's oldest MXIDs reach one hundred million transactions from the wraparound point. And, just as in the XID case, if these warnings are ignored, the system will refuse to generate new MXIDs once there are fewer than three million left until wraparound.

facts.summary: MXID exhaustion is recovered with the same steps, except that running and prepared transactions can be ignored when they cannot be in a multixact, and replication slots do not directly hold back multixact cleanup.
facts.quote: Normal operation when MXIDs are exhausted can be restored in much the same way as when XIDs are exhausted. Follow the same steps in the previous section, but with the following differences: … Running transactions and prepared transactions can be ignored if there is no chance that they might appear in a multixact. … Unlike transaction ID wraparound, replication slots do not directly hold back multixact cleanup.

facts.summary: XID exhaustion blocks all write transactions; MXID exhaustion blocks only writes whose row locks need an MXID.
facts.quote: XID exhaustion will block all write transactions, but MXID exhaustion will only block a subset of write transactions, specifically those that involve row locks that require an MXID.

facts.summary: autovacuum_freeze_max_age is the relfrozenxid age at which a VACUUM is forced to prevent wraparound; the system launches these autovacuums even when autovacuum is disabled.
facts.quote: Specifies the maximum age (in transactions) that a table's pg_class.relfrozenxid field can attain before a VACUUM operation is forced to prevent transaction ID wraparound within the table. Note that the system will launch autovacuum processes to prevent wraparound even when autovacuum is otherwise disabled.

facts.summary: autovacuum_freeze_max_age defaults to 200 million transactions, can only be set at server start, and can be reduced per table through storage parameters.
facts.quote: which is why the default is a relatively low 200 million transactions. This parameter can only be set at server start, but the setting can be reduced for individual tables by changing table storage parameters.

facts.summary: autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age is the relminmxid age that forces a VACUUM against multixact wraparound; default 400 million multixacts, set only at server start.
facts.quote: Specifies the maximum age (in multixacts) that a table's pg_class.relminmxid field can attain before a VACUUM operation is forced to prevent multixact ID wraparound within the table. … which is why the default is a relatively low 400 million multixacts. This parameter can only be set at server start

facts.summary: vacuum_freeze_table_age: VACUUM scans aggressively (every page that may hold unfrozen XIDs or MXIDs) once relfrozenxid reaches this age; default 150 million transactions.
facts.quote: VACUUM performs an aggressive scan if the table's pg_class.relfrozenxid field has reached the age specified by this setting. An aggressive scan differs from a regular VACUUM in that it visits every page that might contain unfrozen XIDs or MXIDs, not just those that might contain dead tuples. The default is 150 million transactions.

facts.summary: vacuum_freeze_table_age accepts zero to two billion, but VACUUM silently limits its effective value to 95% of autovacuum_freeze_max_age.
facts.quote: Although users can set this value anywhere from zero to two billion, VACUUM will silently limit the effective value to 95% of autovacuum_freeze_max_age, so that a periodic manual VACUUM has a chance to run before an anti-wraparound autovacuum is launched for the table.

facts.summary: vacuum_freeze_min_age is the XID cutoff age that decides whether to trigger freezing of a page; default 50 million transactions.
facts.quote: Specifies the cutoff age (in transactions) that VACUUM should use to decide whether to trigger freezing of pages that have an older XID. The default is 50 million transactions.

facts.summary: vacuum_freeze_min_age accepts zero to one billion, but VACUUM silently limits its effective value to half of autovacuum_freeze_max_age.
facts.quote: Although users can set this value anywhere from zero to one billion, VACUUM will silently limit the effective value to half the value of autovacuum_freeze_max_age, so that there is not an unreasonably short time between forced autovacuums.

facts.summary: vacuum_failsafe_age is the relfrozenxid age at which VACUUM takes extraordinary measures, its last resort; it typically triggers during an anti-wraparound autovacuum that has run for some time, but can trigger in any VACUUM.
facts.quote: Specifies the maximum age (in transactions) that a table's pg_class.relfrozenxid field can attain before VACUUM takes extraordinary measures to avoid system-wide transaction ID wraparound failure. This is VACUUM's strategy of last resort. The failsafe typically triggers when an autovacuum to prevent transaction ID wraparound has already been running for some time, though it's possible for the failsafe to trigger during any VACUUM.

facts.summary: When the XID failsafe triggers, cost-based delay stops, non-essential work such as index vacuuming is bypassed, and any Buffer Access Strategy is disabled.
facts.quote: When the failsafe is triggered, any cost-based delay that is in effect will no longer be applied, further non-essential maintenance tasks (such as index vacuuming) are bypassed, and any Buffer Access Strategy in use will be disabled resulting in VACUUM being free to make use of all of shared buffers.

facts.summary: vacuum_failsafe_age defaults to 1.6 billion transactions, accepts zero to 2.1 billion, and is silently raised to no less than 105% of autovacuum_freeze_max_age.
facts.quote: The default is 1.6 billion transactions. Although users can set this value anywhere from zero to 2.1 billion, VACUUM will silently adjust the effective value to no less than 105% of autovacuum_freeze_max_age.

facts.summary: vacuum_multixact_freeze_table_age defaults to 150 million multixacts, accepts zero to two billion, effective value limited to 95% of autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age.
facts.quote: The default is 150 million multixacts. Although users can set this value anywhere from zero to two billion, VACUUM will silently limit the effective value to 95% of autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age

facts.summary: vacuum_multixact_freeze_min_age defaults to 5 million multixacts, accepts zero to one billion, effective value limited to half of autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age.
facts.quote: The default is 5 million multixacts. Although users can set this value anywhere from zero to one billion, VACUUM will silently limit the effective value to half the value of autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age

facts.summary: vacuum_multixact_failsafe_age: when triggered, cost delay stops and non-essential tasks are bypassed (no Buffer Access Strategy clause here); default 1.6 billion multixacts, zero to 2.1 billion, at least 105% of autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age.
facts.quote: When the failsafe is triggered, any cost-based delay that is in effect will no longer be applied, and further non-essential maintenance tasks (such as index vacuuming) are bypassed. … The default is 1.6 billion multixacts. Although users can set this value anywhere from zero to 2.1 billion, VACUUM will silently adjust the effective value to no less than 105% of autovacuum_multixact_freeze_max_age.

facts.summary: vacuum_max_eager_freeze_failure_rate caps the fraction of pages a normal VACUUM may eagerly scan and fail to set all-frozen; 0 disables eager scanning, default 0.03 (3%); successful eager freezes are capped internally at 20%.
facts.quote: Specifies the maximum number of pages (as a fraction of total pages in the relation) that VACUUM may scan and fail to set all-frozen in the visibility map before disabling eager scanning. A value of 0 disables eager scanning altogether. The default is 0.03 (3%). … Successful page freezes are capped internally at 20% of the all-visible but not all-frozen pages in the relation.

facts.summary: GetNewTransactionId's rules: past xidVacLimit force autovacuum, past xidWarnLimit warn, past xidStopLimit refuse transactions unless in single-user mode; the same logic is in GetNewMultiXactId.
facts.quote: If we're past xidVacLimit, start trying to force autovacuum cycles. If we're past xidWarnLimit, start issuing warnings. If we're past xidStopLimit, refuse to execute transactions, unless we are running in single-user mode (which gives an escape hatch to the DBA who somehow got past the earlier defenses). … Note that this coding also appears in GetNewMultiXactId.

facts.summary: Past xidVacLimit the backend signals the postmaster to start the autovacuum launcher only once every 65536 (64K) XIDs.
facts.quote: we issue the autovac request only once per 64K transaction starts. … if (IsUnderPostmaster && (xid % 65536) == 0) SendPostmasterSignal(PMSIGNAL_START_AUTOVAC_LAUNCHER);

facts.summary: The hard stop applies only under the postmaster: it raises ERROR with code ERRCODE_PROGRAM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, and its hint adds a second line about old prepared transactions and stale replication slots.
facts.quote: if (IsUnderPostmaster && TransactionIdFollowsOrEquals(xid, xidStopLimit)) … errcode(ERRCODE_PROGRAM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED), … database is not accepting commands that assign new transaction IDs to avoid wraparound data loss in database … Execute a database-wide VACUUM in that database. … You might also need to commit or roll back old prepared transactions, or drop stale replication slots.

facts.summary: Past xidWarnLimit the WARNING gives the XIDs left (xidWrapLimit minus xid) and a DETAIL percentage computed against MaxTransactionId / 2.
facts.quote: else if (TransactionIdFollowsOrEquals(xid, xidWarnLimit)) … must be vacuumed within %u transactions … Approximately %.2f%% of transaction ID space remains before wraparound. … (double) (xidWrapLimit - xid) / (MaxTransactionId / 2) * 100),

facts.summary: xidWrapLimit, the point of real trouble, is halfway round the XID space from the oldest datfrozenxid: oldest_datfrozenxid + (MaxTransactionId >> 1).
facts.quote: The place where we actually get into deep trouble is halfway around from the oldest potentially-existing XID. … xidWrapLimit = oldest_datfrozenxid + (MaxTransactionId >> 1);

facts.summary: xidStopLimit is xidWrapLimit minus 3,000,000: XID assignment in interactive mode stops within 3M transactions of data loss, leaving room to fix things in a standalone backend.
facts.quote: We'll refuse to continue assigning XIDs in interactive mode once we get within 3M transactions of data loss. This leaves lots of room for the DBA to fool around fixing things in a standalone backend, while not being significant compared to total XID space. … xidStopLimit = xidWrapLimit - 3000000;

facts.summary: The code notes that VACUUM needs an XID when it truncates at wal_level other than minimal, and that VACUUM (ANALYZE) assigns an XID.
facts.quote: VACUUM requires an XID if it truncates at wal_level!=minimal. "VACUUM (ANALYZE)", which a DBA might do by reflex, assigns an XID.

facts.summary: xidWarnLimit is xidWrapLimit minus 100,000,000 (warnings within 100M transactions of data loss) and is deliberately not configurable.
facts.quote: We'll start complaining loudly when we get within 100M transactions of data loss. … No, we're not gonna make this configurable. … xidWarnLimit = xidWrapLimit - 100000000;

facts.summary: xidVacLimit is oldest_datfrozenxid plus autovacuum_freeze_max_age; guc.c keeps that setting in a range that puts xidVacLimit well before xidWarnLimit, and it is a PGC_POSTMASTER parameter.
facts.quote: We'll start trying to force autovacuums when oldest_datfrozenxid gets to be more than autovacuum_freeze_max_age transactions old. … guc.c ensures that autovacuum_freeze_max_age is in a sane range, so that xidVacLimit will be well before xidWarnLimit. … autovacuum_freeze_max_age is a PGC_POSTMASTER parameter … xidVacLimit = oldest_datfrozenxid + autovacuum_freeze_max_age;

facts.summary: Under an MVCC snapshot a tuple is visible iff valid for that snapshot: effects of transactions committed as of the snapshot and earlier commands of the own transaction count; in-progress, later-started transactions and the current command do not.
facts.quote: A tuple is visible iff the tuple is valid for the given MVCC snapshot. Here, we consider the effects of: - all transactions committed as of the time of the given snapshot - previous commands of this transaction Does _not_ include: - transactions shown as in-progress by the snapshot - transactions started after the snapshot was taken - changes made by the current command

facts.summary: An MVCC snapshot never sees XIDs at or above its xmax, sees all older XIDs except those listed in it, and every XID below its xmin is visible; xmin is an optimization to skip the array search.
facts.quote: An MVCC snapshot can never see the effects of XIDs >= xmax. It can see the effects of all older XIDs except those listed in the snapshot. xmin is stored as an optimization to avoid needing to search the XID arrays for most tuples. … TransactionId xmin; /* all XID < xmin are visible to me */ TransactionId xmax; /* all XID >= xmax are invisible to me */

facts.summary: For a normal MVCC snapshot xip lists the transactions in progress when it was taken (empty if taken during recovery), each satisfying xmin <= xip[i] < xmax.
facts.quote: For normal MVCC snapshot this contains the all xact IDs that are in progress, unless the snapshot was taken during recovery in which case it's empty. … note: all ids in xip[] satisfy xmin <= xip[i] < xmax

facts.summary: subxip lists in-progress subtransaction IDs and can overflow (suboverflowed); curcid makes commands of the own transaction with a lower command ID visible.
facts.quote: For non-historic MVCC snapshots, this contains subxact IDs that are in progress (and other transactions that are in progress if taken during recovery). … bool suboverflowed; /* has the subxip array overflowed? */ … CommandId curcid; /* in my xact, CID < curcid are visible */

facts.summary: A non-vacuumable snapshot treats a tuple as visible if it might be visible to any transaction, and as vacuumable if it is surely dead to everyone, judged against an xmin horizon.
facts.quote: A tuple is visible iff the tuple might be visible to some transaction; false if it's surely dead to everyone, i.e., vacuumable. For visibility checks snapshot->min must have been set up with the xmin horizon to use.

conflicts.topic: what a row's insertion XID is compared against to decide visibility
conflicts.note: the manual states it as a comparison with the current transaction's XID; snapshot.h states it against the snapshot's xmin, xmax and in-progress list

conflicts.topic: text of the hard-stop and warning hints
conflicts.note: the manual's example messages show one HINT line; the REL_19_0 source adds a second line about prepared transactions and stale replication slots

conflicts.topic: does the hard stop apply in single-user mode?
conflicts.note: the manual's stop sentence gives no condition; the source applies the stop only under the postmaster, leaving single-user mode as an escape (F21 says single-user mode disables the safeguards)
